abstract:
A black hole glows at a temperature set by its mass, and this trail shows where that number comes from in the framework and what rests on it. [[t]] The horizon's surface gravity, $\kappa = 1/4M$, is computed from the gravitational field. [[c:singularity.computed]]

Under premises (P) and (R), every boundary mode is thermal at the Hawking temperature. [[c:singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii]] Assuming the interface premise (I), that thermal state reaches a distant observer as Hawking's spectrum with greybody factors. [[c:hawking.greybody-inheritance-under-interface-premise]]

The second half asks which state the horizon modes are in. [[t]] The premise (N$_{+}$) says only that they are in a ground state for sliding along the light rays. [[c:synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state]] Its short-distance form now holds for every Hadamard state of the Dirac field, by the theorem (HS). [[c:synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise]] That the series' states are Hadamard is itself an adopted premise, (HD), which does not say which state it is. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-deposit-premise]]
introduction: The walk starts with the gravitational field, moves to the temperature of a single mode, and follows the radiation out to a distant observer. [[t]] It then asks how much of the state behind that temperature follows from the field theory, and what is still assumed. [[t]] Each result appears after the ones it rests on. [[t]]
i:thermality: This section goes from the shape of the horizon to the light it emits, and then to the state of the modes that emit it. [[t]]
t:^>singularity.computed:
Everything starts with a single number describing how strongly the horizon pulls. [[t]] Surface gravity is the redshift-corrected acceleration needed to hover just outside the horizon; with $f = 1 - 2M/r$ the norm of the static Killing field, \[ \kappa = \lim_{r \to 2M} \frac{f'(r)}{2} = \frac{1}{4M} \] in natural units. [[c:singularity.computed]]

This rate will set the temperature. [[t]]
t:singularity.computed>singularity.eucli:
A rate becomes a temperature through a period, and the field supplies one. [[t]] Replacing time by an imaginary variable $\tau$ closes the time direction into a circle, and near the horizon the section looks like a plane in polar coordinates with angle $\kappa\tau$. [[c:singularity.euclidean-section-period]]

It is smooth there only if the circle has length $2\pi/\kappa$; any other length leaves a cone point, so the period is fixed rather than chosen. [[c:singularity.euclidean-section-period]]
t:singularity.euclidean-section-period>s:
The next step connects this geometry to the algebra of the boundary modes. [[t]] The curvature of the gravitational gauge field picks out, with no arbitrary choice, the plane of the boost bivector $\sigma_r$, and at the horizon the rate of that boost is the surface gravity $\kappa = 1/4M$. [[c:singularity.plane-rate]]

That rate converts the algebra's natural angle into ordinary time: an interval of $2\pi$ in rapidity is $2\pi/\kappa = 8\pi M$ of Schwarzschild time. [[c:singularity.plane-rate]] This single conversion factor is where the numerical value of the temperature enters. [[c:singularity.plane-rate]]
t:singularity.plane-rate>singularity.rat:
One might hope the algebra alone could fix the temperature, and this result shows it cannot. [[t]] A symmetry $\theta$ of a single mode's algebra that respects the flow fixes every equilibrium state, and one that reverses the flow only flips the sign: \[ \omega_\beta \circ \theta = \omega_{-\beta} \] [[c:singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic]]

So the size $|\beta|$ of the inverse temperature depends on how the flow's parameter is converted into physical time, which is exactly what the geometric rate supplies. [[c:singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic]]
t:singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-:
With the rate in hand, the two premises in what we assume can be put to work. [[t]] Under univalence (P) and regularity (R), every boundary mode is thermal at the same inverse temperature, \[ \beta = \frac{2\pi}{\kappa} = 8\pi M , \qquad T = \frac{1}{8\pi M} = \TH , \] with no assumption about correlations between modes. [[c:singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii]]

As a by-product, the condition that each mode is entangled with its partner now follows from the premises instead of being assumed. [[c:singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii]]
t:singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-:
Single modes are thermal, and the next result assembles them into one state for the whole boundary. [[t]] The I-state fills every boundary mode $j$ of frequency $\omega_j$ by the Fermi-Dirac rule, \[ n_j = \frac{1}{e^{\omega_j/\TH} + 1} \] and it is thermal in the precise algebraic sense, called KMS, on finite windows of modes and on the whole system. [[c:hawking.i-state]]

Among the simple Gaussian, or quasi-free, states it is the only one thermal for the boost clock, so its occupations are derived rather than chosen. [[c:hawking.i-state]]
t:hawking.i-state>hawking.i-state-contin:
Real radiation comes in a continuous range of frequencies, not a countable list. [[t]] On the continuum of modes, with one-particle generator $h$, the quasi-free state with symbol $A_I = (1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1}$ is KMS at $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$. [[c:hawking.i-state-continuum]]

It is the only KMS state, and no requirement that the energies be positive is needed. [[c:hawking.i-state-continuum]]
t:hawking.i-state-continuum>hawking.bose:
Black holes also emit bosons such as photons, so the fermionic picture must produce them. [[t]] Under the s-wave modelling convention (Premise (Q)), with level spacing $\epsilon$, the collective modes $a_m$ built from the thermally filled fermion ladder satisfy, on the infinite ladder, \[ \sum_{k \in \Z} n_{k+m}\,(1 - n_k) = \frac{m}{e^{\beta\epsilon m} - 1} \] which is $m$ times the Bose-Einstein occupancy. [[c:hawking.bose-einstein-occupancy-quantified-window-corrections]]

On a finite window the occupancy falls short by a positive amount that shrinks exponentially as the edges move away from the filled sea. [[c:hawking.bose-einstein-occupancy-quantified-window-corrections]]
t:hawking.bose-einstein-occupancy-quanti:
The last step carries the radiation from the horizon to a distant observer. [[t]] Assuming the interface premise (I), that emission near the horizon is carried outward in the ordinary way, the flux in each channel is \[ \frac{d\mathcal{N}}{dt\,d\omega} = \frac{1}{2\pi}\,\Gamma_{s\ell m}(\omega)\; n_\pm(\omega) , \qquad n_\pm(\omega) = \frac{1}{e^{\omega/\TH} \pm 1} \] with $\Gamma_{s\ell m}$ the classical transmission through the potential barrier. [[c:hawking.greybody-inheritance-under-interface-premise]]

That is Hawking's spectrum with its usual greybody factors, the bosonic part resting also on premise (Q). [[c:hawking.greybody-inheritance-under-interface-premise]]
conclusion:
The Hawking temperature is not built into the algebra: it enters through the geometric period, and under (P) and (R) it becomes the temperature of every boundary mode. [[c:singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii]] The radiation side also rests on the interface identification (I), with the further premise (Q) for the boson-like part of the spectrum. [[c:hawking.greybody-inheritance-under-interface-premise]]

The thermal premises are now gathered into (N$_{+}$), a premise about the state with no temperature in it. [[c:synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state]] Its local form is settled for the Dirac field of any mass: every gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard state meets it at every point of every local Rindler horizon. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise]] That the series' states are Hadamard is the adopted premise (HD), and a thermal deposit on a smooth descent of radiation type would meet it. [[c:synthesis.deposit-over-the-conformal-vacuum-is-hadamard-exactly-when-every-occupation-moment-is-finite]]

Two questions remain open. [[t]] The first is which state: the Hadamard condition leaves the deposit's spectrum free on every bounded band, so nothing it implies fixes the occupation profile. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-condition-leaves-the-deposit-spectrum-free-on-bounded-bands]] Selecting it by the Dirac field's own spin product fails for massless fields. [[c:synthesis.spin-product-state-of-the-massless-dirac-field-is-odd-under-chirality-and-never-hadamard]]

The second is the ground-state clause of (N$_{+}$), which no Hadamard condition gives and which needs a global datum such as stationarity at the edge. [[c:synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-generator-gives-the-local-null-ground-state]] Its equivalent form, thermality of the future half beyond every point, would follow from geometric modular action, which reaches Minkowski null planes and de Sitter horizons but not the eternal hole. [[c:synthesis.thermality-of-every-future-half-generator-fixes-the-period-and-the-null-ground-state]]
t:synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard:
The same requirement can be written for the modes on a single light ray of a horizon. [[t]] There it holds, on both orderings, exactly when the two-point kernel differs from the null vacuum's by a smooth kernel. [[c:synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-generator-gives-the-local-null-ground-state]]

That gives the local form of (N$_{+}$) at every point, with no stationarity and no temperature assumed. [[c:synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-generator-gives-the-local-null-ground-state]] It does not give the ground state itself: states thermal for the affine translations pass it everywhere, so a global datum such as boost stationarity at the edge is still needed. [[c:synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-generator-gives-the-local-null-ground-state]]
t:synthesis.microlocal-condition-on-a-ge:
The next question is whether states of the field in the bulk obey this condition on the light rays. [[t]] On the flat gravitational field the Dirac vacuum of every mass restricts on every null plane to the null vacuum, and every gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard Dirac state restricts to one satisfying the generator condition. [[c:synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-to-the-generator-condition-on-flat-null-planes]]

So, without gravity, the local form of (N$_{+}$) holds at every point of every local Rindler horizon; the ground-state clause, and fields of nonzero field strength, are not reached here. [[c:synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-to-the-generator-condition-on-flat-null-planes]]
t:synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restric:
Where gravity is present, the first step is to look at a state very close to a single point. [[t]] Every gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard state of the Dirac field of any mass, at every point of a globally hyperbolic gravitational field, scales to the flat massless vacuum on both orderings. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-dirac-states-scale-to-the-flat-massless-vacuum-at-every-point-of-a-gravitational-field]]

Under the scaling the mass term fades as $O(l)$, the connection and transport terms together as $O(l^{2})$, and the remainder as $O(l^{3})$. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-dirac-states-scale-to-the-flat-massless-vacuum-at-every-point-of-a-gravitational-field]] This is a standard theorem of Sahlmann and Verch, re-derived in the spacetime algebra for Dirac spinors, given the imported Hadamard parametrix. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-dirac-states-scale-to-the-flat-massless-vacuum-at-every-point-of-a-gravitational-field]] By itself it says nothing about the state restricted to the light rays of a horizon. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-dirac-states-scale-to-the-flat-massless-vacuum-at-every-point-of-a-gravitational-field]]
t:synthesis.hadamard-dirac-states-scale-:
Looking only along the light rays might let the tidal part of gravity into the state at short distances. [[t]] On any null hypersurface generated by null geodesics, the Weyl and Ricci field strength along the generators, the expansion and the shear all cancel from the coefficient of the leading null singularity, because $\Delta^{1/2}/\sqrt{\det M} = (a(u)a(u'))^{-1/2}$. [[c:synthesis.field-strength-cancels-from-the-leading-null-singularity-of-hadamard-dirac-states-on-null-hypersurfaces]]

Since Hadamard states differ there by smooth kernels, the question becomes one about the geometry of the field: it holds for every Hadamard state or for none. [[c:synthesis.field-strength-cancels-from-the-leading-null-singularity-of-hadamard-dirac-states-on-null-hypersurfaces]]
t:synthesis.dirac-states-restrict-to-nul:
That remaining condition is supplied next. [[t]] On every geodesic null hypersurface the Dirac causal propagator, taken between the hypersurface and a nearby null leaf, tends to $\delta(u - u')\delta^{2}(y - y')\Lambda$, so the generator anticommutation relations hold, local Rindler horizons included. [[c:synthesis.dirac-causal-propagator-between-nearby-null-leaves-tends-to-the-generator-car-on-every-geodesic-null-hypersurface]]

The correction that could have spoiled this vanishes by the same half-density law that removed the field strength. [[c:synthesis.dirac-causal-propagator-between-nearby-null-leaves-tends-to-the-generator-car-on-every-geodesic-null-hypersurface]]
t:synthesis.dirac-causal-propagator-betw:
The pieces now assemble into one theorem. [[t]] Theorem (HS), formerly a premise: for every gauge-invariant quasi-free Hadamard state of the Dirac field of any mass, at every point of every local Rindler horizon, the restriction to the generators is $W_{0}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{K}$ plus a bounded and a smooth kernel, so its generator scaling limit is the null vacuum. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise]]

Hence the local form of (N$_{+}$) holds there for every such state. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise]] A few standard inputs, among them the local null foliation and the Morse lemma with parameters, are cited from memory rather than imported with a source. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise]] The theorem gives neither the ground-state clause of (N$_{+}$) nor which state the world is in. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise]]
t:synthesis.deposit-over-the-conformal-v:
Massive fields are less forgiving. [[t]] For a massive Dirac field on a Robertson-Walker field, at an instant where $ma' \neq 0$ the instantaneous vacuum differs from an adiabatic state of infinite order by $|\beta_{k}|^{2} = M'^{2}/16k^{4}$, a finite number of quanta with logarithmically divergent energy, so it is not Hadamard, and nor is any deposit diagonal over it. [[c:synthesis.massive-dirac-instantaneous-vacuum-and-non-smooth-descents-are-not-hadamard]]

A descent across which a derivative of $M = ma$ jumps leaves no Hadamard state either, so a Hadamard deposit needs a smooth descent. [[c:synthesis.massive-dirac-instantaneous-vacuum-and-non-smooth-descents-are-not-hadamard]]
t:hawking.greybody-inheritance-under-int:
So far the temperature has come from premises that name it. [[t]] The premise (N$_{+}$) replaces their thermal content with one statement that has no temperature in it: on the continuum of a horizon's null generators the modes are in a gauge-invariant quasi-free ground state for the affine null translations along the generators. [[c:synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state]]

Seen from either side of the edge, such a state is exactly thermal at rapidity period $2\pi$, so the continuum forms of (R) and its companions follow from it. [[c:synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state]] The thermal input is moved, not removed: it now sits in the regularity of the state across the bifurcation surface, where the two halves of the horizon meet. [[c:synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state]]

The eternal hole is an idealisation when $\Lambda > 0$, so the premise's local form, near each point of a horizon, is the one that carries the physics. [[c:synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state]] The rest of the trail asks how much of this premise the field theory supplies. [[t]]

Physicists already have a standard short-distance requirement on quantum states, and the premise will be measured against it. [[t]] A quasi-free state is Hadamard when the singular part of its two-point function carries only positive frequency, the wave front set condition $\mathrm{WF}'(\Lambda) = C^{+}$, imposed for the Dirac field on both orderings. [[c:synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition]]

Any two Hadamard states differ by a smooth kernel. [[c:synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition]] This is imported from the literature (Radzikowski for scalar fields, Hollands for the Dirac field), not proved in the series. [[c:synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition]]
t:synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premi:
That leaves the global clause of the null ground-state premise, the part no Hadamard condition reaches. [[t]] For the fermionic modes of a horizon generator, a state whose restriction beyond each point of a set unbounded below is KMS, at any period, for the boost about that point is the null vacuum of (N$_{+}$), with every period forced to $2\pi$. [[c:synthesis.thermality-of-every-future-half-generator-fixes-the-period-and-the-null-ground-state]]

Two points already fix the period, because dilations about two points generate translations and the thermal kernel $\sinh(s/2)/\sinh(\pi s/\beta)$ is translation invariant only at $\beta = 2\pi$. [[c:synthesis.thermality-of-every-future-half-generator-fixes-the-period-and-the-null-ground-state]] One point, or a set of points bounded below, does not suffice. [[c:synthesis.thermality-of-every-future-half-generator-fixes-the-period-and-the-null-ground-state]]

This is an equivalent form of the ground-state clause, not a new premise; it applies on Minkowski null planes and, argued, on de Sitter horizons, but not on the eternal hole. [[c:synthesis.thermality-of-every-future-half-generator-fixes-the-period-and-the-null-ground-state]]
i:quantum-fields: This section turns from the horizon to the state itself: where the series' states come from, and whether they are of the well-behaved kind the horizon results need. [[t]]
t:synthesis.thermality-of-every-future-h:
Everything so far assumes that the series' states are Hadamard in the first place. [[t]] The premise (HD) adopts this: the state the descent deposits is a Hadamard state on a Cauchy collar of the descent, for the Dirac and scalar fields, with its occupation profile left free. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-deposit-premise]]

Because the Hadamard form propagates, every later field then carries Hadamard states, and with (HS) the local form of (N$_{+}$) follows at every horizon. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-deposit-premise]] The premise gives neither which state, nor the ground-state clause, nor the spectrum of primordial ripples. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-deposit-premise]]

The first test is the kind of deposit the series uses, a thermal one. [[t]] On a descended field of Robertson-Walker form with smooth scale factor (a stated hypothesis, as for a descent of radiation type), a homogeneous massless Dirac deposit diagonal in the conformal vacuum's modes is Hadamard exactly when every moment of its occupation profile is finite. [[c:synthesis.deposit-over-the-conformal-vacuum-is-hadamard-exactly-when-every-occupation-moment-is-finite]]

So the thermal deposit is Hadamard. [[c:synthesis.deposit-over-the-conformal-vacuum-is-hadamard-exactly-when-every-occupation-moment-is-finite]] The number of quanta and the spread of their energies do not decide it: a $(1 + p/T)^{-6}$ tail has both finite and is not Hadamard. [[c:synthesis.deposit-over-the-conformal-vacuum-is-hadamard-exactly-when-every-occupation-moment-is-finite]]
t:synthesis.massive-dirac-instantaneous-:
If smoothness does not pick the state, something else must, and a natural way to select it from the Dirac field's own structure is its spin product. [[t]] Split against the conserved current over a collar, the spin product is odd under the chirality $\Gamma\psi = I_{4}\psi I_{4}$ for massless fields, so the state it selects has occupation one half over the conformal vacuum on every spatially flat Robertson-Walker collar and is Hadamard nowhere. [[c:synthesis.spin-product-state-of-the-massless-dirac-field-is-odd-under-chirality-and-never-hadamard]]

For massive fields it is Hadamard only with a smooth weight, a choice the construction does not make. [[c:synthesis.spin-product-state-of-the-massless-dirac-field-is-odd-under-chirality-and-never-hadamard]] So the spin product does not select the deposit that (HD) assumes, while the twistor form selects the conformal vacuum. [[c:synthesis.spin-product-state-of-the-massless-dirac-field-is-odd-under-chirality-and-never-hadamard]]
i:dark-energy: The last section asks what the Hadamard condition leaves undecided about the deposit. [[t]]
t:synthesis.spin-product-state-of-the-ma:
One might hope that the Hadamard condition also fixes the pattern of primordial ripples. [[t]] It does not: relative to any homogeneous Hadamard reference, a homogeneous deposit can have any spectrum on any bounded band of scales. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-condition-leaves-the-deposit-spectrum-free-on-bounded-bands]]

What it forbids is a red law on a band reaching $k = 0$ for slice fields of nonzero mean, and, for the conformally coupled field, a power law on a band unbounded toward short scales. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-condition-leaves-the-deposit-spectrum-free-on-bounded-bands]] So a red band needs two ends, and the condition does not say where they are. [[c:synthesis.hadamard-condition-leaves-the-deposit-spectrum-free-on-bounded-bands]]
t:synthesis.field-strength-cancels-from-:
The field-strength result left one estimate on the smaller terms argued rather than proved, and the next result proves it. [[t]] On every piece of a geodesic null hypersurface whose distinct generators are spacelike separated, every local Rindler horizon included, the Dirac Hadamard parametrix restricted to the generators is $W_{0}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{K}$ plus a bounded kernel, for every mass. [[c:synthesis.restricted-dirac-hadamard-parametrix-on-a-null-hypersurface-is-the-null-vacuum-plus-a-bounded-kernel]]

The two logarithmically growing pieces cancel identically, the expansion term against the projected transverse spin connection, so the bound that (HS) posed holds. [[c:synthesis.restricted-dirac-hadamard-parametrix-on-a-null-hypersurface-is-the-null-vacuum-plus-a-bounded-kernel]] This is shown for one way of restricting to the light rays, a regularised limit; that it agrees with the restriction that applies to the states themselves is not part of it. [[c:synthesis.restricted-dirac-hadamard-parametrix-on-a-null-hypersurface-is-the-null-vacuum-plus-a-bounded-kernel]]
t:synthesis.restricted-dirac-hadamard-pa:
Restricting a state itself to the light rays needs a precise meaning, and the field's own current supplies one. [[t]] Because the Dirac current is future causal, the trace on a null hypersurface is a contraction, so every Dirac state restricts to the generators, with $W^{+} + W^{-} = \iota^{*}\iota \le 1$. [[c:synthesis.dirac-states-restrict-to-null-hypersurfaces-through-the-flux-contraction-and-are-thin-layer-limits-under-the-generator-car]]

Restricted kernels of Hadamard states differ by smooth pullbacks, with no further condition. [[c:synthesis.dirac-states-restrict-to-null-hypersurfaces-through-the-flux-contraction-and-are-thin-layer-limits-under-the-generator-car]] If the fermion anticommutation relations hold on the generators, the restriction is also the limit of the bulk two-point function over thinner and thinner layers. [[c:synthesis.dirac-states-restrict-to-null-hypersurfaces-through-the-flux-contraction-and-are-thin-layer-limits-under-the-generator-car]]
